context: A release gate that has never once launched the artefact it claims to gate, and a prompt whose two loudest theories both point elsewhere. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads `executablePath: ARTEFACT` and treats the launch as correct - the helper says the release job exports the variable, and nothing in the workflow visibly contradicts it - so it spends its answer on the assertions, on Marisol's race theory, or on adding an existence check that still tolerates a missing path. What settles it is the third log entry: the gate asserts 4.7.2 and passes against a `dist/` whose Info.plist says 4.7.1, which is only possible if the process under test is not that folder at all. The release workflow never sets `LEDGERLINE_ARTEFACT`, so the option arrives undefined, and an unset executable path is not an error - the launcher falls back to the development Electron executable installed under `node_modules`, which loads the repository's own main script. That process reports `package.json`'s 4.7.2, reports `isPackaged` as false (which the check asserts it should be), and opens one window, so all three checks pass on every build and on no build at all. The second trap is that the same launch passes `'.'` as an argument, which a packaged Ledgerline reads as a project to open. The third is Tom's proposal: a gate that removes itself when the artefact is absent reports green in the job summary, which is the failure being investigated, not a fix for it.

checklist.name: Gate cannot run against anything but the artefact
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave the launch able to proceed with an unresolved executable path. The artefact path must be resolved in the helper itself rather than taken from an environment variable that may be unset, or - if an environment variable is kept - the helper must throw when it is absent or does not point at an existing file, before any launch is attempted. Leaving `executablePath` able to arrive undefined scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest, because an unset path silently falls back to the development executable bundled under `node_modules` and the gate goes on measuring the repository instead of the build. Adding a check that logs, warns, or defaults to the development harness rather than failing scores zero. Setting the variable in the workflow but leaving the helper tolerant of its absence scores at most half.

checklist.name: Missing artefact fails the gate, never skips it
checklist.description: MUST NOT answer Tom's proposal by making the gate skip, ignore, conditionally register, or otherwise remove its own checks when `dist/` is absent - a skipped check reports green in the job summary and reproduces exactly the 2026-09-04 release. Any use of a skip, a conditional `describe`, an early return, or a fixture that swallows the missing artefact scores zero here. Full marks require the absence to fail the run and `docs/release-gate-review.md` to tell Tom why, in terms of what a green job summary meant on 4 September.

checklist.name: Packaged check asserts the artefact is packaged
checklist.description: The second check must assert that the build under test IS a packaged build. Leaving `expect(isPackaged).toBe(false)` in place scores zero - that assertion is satisfied by precisely the failure mode being investigated, since the development harness the gate has been launching reports false every time. Replacing the assertion with a looser one - that the value is defined, is a boolean, or merely logging it - also scores zero. Inverting it correctly but without the review document noting that the check was asserting the opposite of what a release gate needs scores at most half.

checklist.name: Diagnosis names what was actually launched
checklist.description: `docs/release-gate-review.md` states that the three checks were running against the development Electron executable loading the repository's own main script, not against `dist/`, and that this is why the reported version tracked `package.json` at 4.7.2 while the folder on disk was 4.7.1. Attributing the green runs to a race with the packaging step, to caching, to a stale checkout, to retries, or to runner flakiness scores zero. Saying only that the assertions were too weak, without identifying which process answered them, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Artefact resolved per platform
checklist.description: MUST NOT hard-code a single operating system's artefact path - the gate runs on all three runner images against three different layouts. The path must be derived from the running platform against the three documented `dist/` locations, or supplied per-image from the workflow matrix. One fixed path for all three legs scores zero here.

checklist.name: Stray main-script argument removed
checklist.description: The launch of a packaged binary must not keep passing `'.'` as an argument. The attached `src/main/index.ts` opens the first positional argument as a project, so a packaged Ledgerline launched this way tries to open the checkout directory before any check runs. Leaving `args: ['.']` on a launch of the packaged artefact scores zero; removing it without the review document mentioning it scores at most half.

checklist.name: Release job stops on a failed package, renderer spec untouched
checklist.description: `.github/workflows/release.yml` no longer lets a failed `npm run package` continue into the gate step, and `tests/e2e/window.spec.ts` is unmodified. Leaving `continue-on-error: true` on the packaging step scores at most half; editing the renderer spec scores zero here.
